children.name: subjects
comments:
max_len="16" is 16 usable characters, so 17 bytes of storage (§8.2).
             The value carries a double quote, a backslash and a non-ASCII
             character — the three things a C++ string literal must escape
             (§13.2) — and is 15 characters, so it fits without truncation.

Bound by three objects and one draw-call element, so its observer
             count is 3 + 1 frame-dirty = 4 (§13.5, [D-21]).

comments: A U8G2 built-in: referenced, never compiled (§14.1).

children.name: styles
comments:
Overrides the global `body`: one ui_style_body, one pool slot, which
             is how mangle.ts keys it and how the capacity was counted.

children.name: view
comments: No object: nothing refers to it and it carries no state (§13.5).
Three objects observing `level` ...

... and one draw-call element, which costs the subject exactly one
             frame-dirty observer however many such elements there are (§13.5).

`scroll_px_per_sec` is a non-coordinate `int` property written as an
             expression: it must reach emission as the literal 20 (§13.2).

children.name: api
comments:
`bitmap_mode` is NOT declared here: u8g2gl_obj declares it identically
         and every element inherits it. A redeclaration would be a second
         spelling of one property, which is what [D-17] exists to prevent.

children.name: subjects
comments: §13.12's subjects.

Read only by draw calls on the gauges screen, so each costs exactly
             one frame-dirty observer and no pool slot (§13.5, [D-21]).
Drives the panel composite's hidden flag.

The bounds screen (PR-04 WO10b): a position bound inside a
             container and on the screen, and an int drawn through a format.

children.name: styles
comments:
The bounds screen: a style whose font an element's own font= and
             style_font override must both beat (§10), and which sets font_mode,
             so the editor applies a style property only u8g2gl_obj declares.

children.name: fonts
comments:
PR-04 WO14: one of the 522 U8G2 fonts whose name carries capitals.
             A <builtin>'s name is a U8G2 symbol, not a name the author chose, so
             it is exempt from §13.4's lowercase rule (owner's ruling,
             2026-09-28) and the alias spells it verbatim. Compiled and drawn on
             the bounds screen, so the exemption is proved end to end rather than
             only in the validator.

PR-04b WO3b item 3: <bdf> in the committed fixture, compiled,
             linked against real U8G2 and measured
             (test/test_bdf_real_u8g2.cpp). U8G2's own public-domain 4x6.bdf,
             filtered to ASCII — assets/fonts/LICENSE quotes its BDF COPYRIGHT
             line.

A hand-written MIT fixture (header comment in the BDF itself) with
             no `range`, proving the absent-range fix (WO3 item 1): a glyph
             below 0x20, one in ASCII, and one above 0xFF (U+2190) all compile
             and reach the screen. No licence file beside it — none needed.

children.name: images
comments:
PR-04b WO4: <convert>, PNG to XBM at generate time. Drawn on the
             bounds screen, compiled, and given to the editor host, so a converted
             image is proved end to end exactly as an <xbm> is. The PNG is
             produced by cli/test/fixtures/make-fixture-logo.ts (byte-stable);
             dithered, so the error-diffusion path is what the C++ suite builds.

children.name: view
comments: Ruling 1: bound positions are container-relative.
PR-04b WO4: a <convert> image, drawn like any bitmap.
...and on the screen, a bound position is its value (no literal x).
An int subject drawn through its format.

Ruling 3: the element's own font= wins over the named style's font;
             the style's align and font_mode, which it does not set, still apply.

...and so does an inline style_* override: right, not the style's
             center.

PR-04 WO14: a font whose U8G2 name carries capitals. It exists to be
             compiled: the alias ui_font_u8g2_font_helvR08_tr is declared in
             ui.hpp, defined in ui_fonts.cpp and passed to set_font() here, and
             the three spellings must agree or this unit will not build.

PR-04b WO3b item 3/5: <bdf> fonts, drawn exactly as a <builtin>
             is — set_font takes the same ui_font_* pointer either way, so
             this is what proves emission goes through the emitter for a
             compiled font too, on firmware and in the editor host alike.

children.name: view
comments:
§8.4's own example: a bound width and no width attribute at all. A
             draw call, so the width is read from the subject at draw time.
A non-default segment, which needs the manifest's emit= pattern.

Hidden until show_panel is true. Its draw-call child and its object
             child must both stay undrawn while it is hidden.
An object hidden outright: the render wrapper must skip it.
A draw call with its own bound hidden flag.
